records.source_meaning: The Port Worker says it looks as though the ship still has not returned. Preserve uncertainty andnot-yet sense without inventing a waiting duration,thief location orevent condition.
records.fresh_source_gloss: The Port Worker says it looks as though the ship still has not returned. Preserve uncertainty andnot-yet sense without inventing a waiting duration,thief location orevent condition.
records.whole_exchange_context:
B161 andB162 contain separate identical Port Worker utterances:it appears the ship has not returned yet. Keep the appearance/uncertainty andstill/not-yet sense. Their neighboring source B160 loss report andB163 return report support ship reference,not a fixed waiting time or known thief location. Do not collapse two source keys or infer their event conditions from their identical prose.
B163 is the complete return/confrontation/recruitment exchange. The Port Worker urgently tells the admiral the ship is back;Lil reacts,andoptional Angelo disbelieves with source Mamma mia. The worker points to the unmistakable ship. The newcomer shouts exuberantly about the vast sea andthe morning's fun,with repeated Yahoo-type cheers. Lil demands to know what he is doing with her ship;Camille orders him off. He insists he found it lying around. Camille rejects that absurd defense. Optional Angelo asks whether his brain has turned to strawberry jam,setting up the source name joke. The newcomer insists the ship looked lonely andabandoned in the harbor,so kindhearted Jam picked it up;he explicitly spells J-A-M andcheers. These are his self-serving assertions,not narrator confirmation that the ship was abandoned. Optional Angelo notices the Jam/brain-jam connection andtrails off;do not finish his thought into a new diagnosis.
Lil asks how merely finding a ship let him take it out to sea. His vague this-and-that/just-somehow answer andanother cheer contrast with her surprise that he did it alone. Camille tentatively calls him a possible genius. Lil asks what he would have done if unable to return. He tut-tuts,announces an aphorism about determination making things possible,cheers andapproves his own judgment. Optional Fernando mutters that someone troublesome has appeared. Lil scolds the repeated cheer. Jam boasts in exaggerated self-important language andproclaims a compressed intense-short-life motto,opposing it to a timid narrow long life. Preserve the deliberate contrast andhis odd verbal performance;do not turn it into an attributed philosophy,religion,national biography or new literal suicide/death plan. Optional Angelo wants to hand him to the guards. Camille instead asks FI to invite him. Optional Fernando sputters Camille's name;Lil objects;optional Angelo asks if Camille's brain has become strawberry jam too. Camille says the man is outrageous butamazing,able to set sail alone,andthe strangest person he has met,then pleads for agreement. Lil gives in,teasing that their navigators are all strange anyway. Optional Angelo protests that she looked at him when saying it;Camille's calming reply is in that same optional branch. Keep these speaker opinions andfamiliar jabs rather than narrator diagnoses.
Camille independently invites Jam to travel together. Jam makes a show of weighing the choice,uses an English-sounding Just a moment andasks for two seconds. The stated two seconds is spoken comedy,not proof of the source native pause operand's unit. He announces readiness;Camille asks if he has decided. Jam declares he will not go andwishes them a good trip. Lil's startled wait leads him to reveal that refusal was a joke,thank them with the source French Merci andcelebrate the reaction. Lil questions the joke. Jam then explicitly asks to be taken along andreintroduces his full name. The original catalogue spells actor11 Jam Jack Ludwyan;bind its current original native consumer andexisting naming policy before authoring,without guessing another full-name spelling. Preserve short Jam with the explicit J-A-M spelling andstrawberry-jam play. Mamma mia,Merci/Just a moment andhis repeated cheer are source-supported verbal choices;add no nationality or romance. Use approved Camille,Angelo andFernando,withone runtime FI. Eight membership sites,six Angelo/two Fernando,32relative containers,one A000,source C283,4679/4622/4695/45FF/0514/4634/6005,resource sites,the two-byte2000 pause,andall four ends across three blocks require their own native/reference/display checks. B161/B162 each have source C200. No natural event eligibility,earned ship recovery/recruitment,source port,elapsed search time orhardware/playthrough claim is available from extraction. The full wider editorial goal remains open.

records.whole_exchange_context:
B161 andB162 contain separate identical Port Worker utterances:it appears the ship has not returned yet. Keep the appearance/uncertainty andstill/not-yet sense. Their neighboring source B160 loss report andB163 return report support ship reference,not a fixed waiting time or known thief location. Do not collapse two source keys or infer their event conditions from their identical prose.
B163 is the complete return/confrontation/recruitment exchange. The Port Worker urgently tells the admiral the ship is back;Lil reacts,andoptional Angelo disbelieves with source Mamma mia. The worker points to the unmistakable ship. The newcomer shouts exuberantly about the vast sea andthe morning's fun,with repeated Yahoo-type cheers. Lil demands to know what he is doing with her ship;Camille orders him off. He insists he found it lying around. Camille rejects that absurd defense. Optional Angelo asks whether his brain has turned to strawberry jam,setting up the source name joke. The newcomer insists the ship looked lonely andabandoned in the harbor,so kindhearted Jam picked it up;he explicitly spells J-A-M andcheers. These are his self-serving assertions,not narrator confirmation that the ship was abandoned. Optional Angelo notices the Jam/brain-jam connection andtrails off;do not finish his thought into a new diagnosis.
Lil asks how merely finding a ship let him take it out to sea. His vague this-and-that/just-somehow answer andanother cheer contrast with her surprise that he did it alone. Camille tentatively calls him a possible genius. Lil asks what he would have done if unable to return. He tut-tuts,announces an aphorism about determination making things possible,cheers andapproves his own judgment. Optional Fernando mutters that someone troublesome has appeared. Lil scolds the repeated cheer. Jam boasts in exaggerated self-important language andproclaims a compressed intense-short-life motto,opposing it to a timid narrow long life. Preserve the deliberate contrast andhis odd verbal performance;do not turn it into an attributed philosophy,religion,national biography or new literal suicide/death plan. Optional Angelo wants to hand him to the guards. Camille instead asks FI to invite him. Optional Fernando sputters Camille's name;Lil objects;optional Angelo asks if Camille's brain has become strawberry jam too. Camille says the man is outrageous butamazing,able to set sail alone,andthe strangest person he has met,then pleads for agreement. Lil gives in,teasing that their navigators are all strange anyway. Optional Angelo protests that she looked at him when saying it;Camille's calming reply is in that same optional branch. Keep these speaker opinions andfamiliar jabs rather than narrator diagnoses.
